Key Takeaways

Palo Alto Networks rose 6.5% today, CrowdStrike rose 6.7%, Okta rose 5%, Cloudflare rose 6% and Zscaler rose 4%, after an Evercore ISI survey of cybersecurity channel partners found security budgets getting stronger.

The rally started Wednesday, when the PHP Foundation disclosed critical flaws found with AI's help and Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora warned more are coming.

Analysts expect Palo Alto's revenue to grow 23% in the fiscal year ending July 2027, but its normalized EPS to grow only 9% as its share count rises.

Palo Alto traded at 85x forward earnings before today's move, with estimates already at the top of guidance, so its next report has to show the spending.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) stock is up 6.5% today, and the cybersecurity group is up with it: CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) is up 6.7%, Okta (OKTA:NASDAQ) 5%, Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) 6% and Zscaler (ZS:NASDAQ) 4%.

The trigger: a reseller survey showing security budgets getting stronger into year-end, in a week already dominated by a security scare.

Resellers are seeing the spending

Security stocks started rallying on Wednesday after the PHP Foundation disclosed critical flaws, found with AI's help, in code much of the web runs on. That afternoon, Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora told the TBPN podcast: "We're gonna see more of these, not less."

This morning, Evercore ISI's quarterly survey of cybersecurity channel partners added a demand read on top of that. Partners resell and install the products, so they see purchases first. They described:

Budgets getting stronger into year-end

Healthy pipelines, with no sign of demand dropping off

Spending on securing data and AI, identities and cloud environments

Okta had the strongest pipeline momentum of any vendor surveyed, and Evercore named it one of two stocks to highlight.

Cybersecurity stocks

Cybersecurity names were among the week's strong performers after an emergency security update for PHP, the programming language used by roughly 70% of websites worldwide, triggered a global alert.

Okta led the moves with a 14% gain over the week, followed by Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike, both up 11%, and Cloudflare, up 9%.

Meta Platforms

Meta fell 7% on Thursday and is down 9.1% over the week after Wednesday's post-close results, with a surprise plan to issue a new class of non-voting stock overshadowing stronger-than-expected third-quarter revenue.

The company's special committee said in its filing that the move was motivated not only by keeping CEO Mark Zuckerberg in California but also by "an increasingly challenging environment for raising capital," citing recent and anticipated raises at Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI to fund the same AI growth.

The committee added that while Meta has sufficient resources for current needs, it would be prudent to act before more companies absorb available capital in the market. The Class C shares are intended for equity offerings from time to time and could be available as early as the end of 2026.

Tesla and SpaceX

Tesla gained 4.6% over the week, and SpaceX added 0.6% after both reported results and confirmed they are examining a tie-up.

Cloudflare's stock has surged over the past few years as investors have latched onto its role in web security and edge computing. With the shares now around US$303.61, the open question is whether that price tag is still supported by its sales base.

Cloudflare has delivered a very large 3 year share price gain of about 4.5x, which makes the gap between its long term share performance and its underlying revenue scale an important issue to examine.

The company's rapid response to the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and ongoing work to support AI driven internet traffic can influence how investors think about future top line potential relative to current P/S levels.

The analysts covering Cloudflare have run their own numbers. See what analysts think Cloudflare's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether Cloudflare's recent share price, after that strong multi year run and a busy stretch of security and AI related announcements, is justified by its sales when compared with the Fair Ratio benchmark.

If you want to test the same sales based valuation question across more AI focused infrastructure players, line Cloudflare up against the 55 AI infrastructure stocks.

Does Cloudflare Look Pricey on Sales?

The P/S lens fits Cloudflare because sales, not earnings, are the cleaner anchor for a business still reinvesting heavily. On this yardstick, the stock trades on a P/S of 43.0x, which is far above both the IT sector average of 2.0x and the 13.8x peer group level for similar infrastructure and security players. A tailored Fair Ratio that blends Cloudflare's growth profile, margin structure, size and risk highlights this as a rich valuation, with the current multiple sitting meaningfully above that benchmark. In other words, the market is already paying a steep price for its revenue base.

The PHP2Shell response and the positive reaction it triggered help explain why investors are willing to ascribe such a premium to Cloudflare's security and AI traffic franchise. Even so, the gap to sector and peer norms still leaves little room for missteps on execution or demand. For anyone weighing the stock today, the key question is whether that 43.0x P/S can be supported by future sales quality and durability, or whether expectations have run too far ahead of the underlying revenue scale. Key Takeaways

Palo Alto Networks shares rose 3% today after Deutsche Bank named it one of three standouts among companies set to gain from rising AI usage, while the Nasdaq fell about 2%.

CEO Nikesh Arora warned that more AI-found flaws like this week's PHP bug are coming, and Cloudflare rose [4%] as the cybersecurity rally carried on.

When AI finds flaws faster, companies have to spend more to defend against them, and that makes Palo Alto a hedge against AI's risks.

The stock already reflects a lot of that demand, with its forward P/E well above its five-year average.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) shares are up 3% today, while the Nasdaq is down about 2%.

Before the open, Deutsche Bank named Palo Alto one of three standouts, along with Snowflake and CrowdStrike, among companies set to gain from rising AI token usage. The bank's reasoning is that expanding data flows, digital identities and attack surfaces support demand for cybersecurity.

AI is finding the holes

On Wednesday, the PHP Foundation disclosed two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language behind nearly 70% of websites, and issued an emergency patch. Researchers found the bugs partly with an OpenAI model.

Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora went on the TBPN podcast Wednesday afternoon with a warning: "We're gonna see more of these, not less."

He said Palo Alto's own scan found 22 million places where the PHP flaw persists. He added that whatever today's AI models miss "will definitely be found three months from now with the next model."

title: Why Is Zscaler Stock Going Up?
detail:
Why Is Zscaler Stock Going Up?
Trefis Team

Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Zscaler (ZS) rose 7.8% on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, outpacing a 0.6% gain for the S&P 500. Benzinga reported that shares climbed that day after DA Davidson began covering Zscaler with a Neutral rating and a $215 price target. The stock had closed about where that target sat the day before, only to finish Wednesday about 8% above it. So what are buyers getting from Zscaler's business at the higher price?

Buyers Pay A Premium For Zscaler's Growth

At the October 21 close, Zscaler stock traded at 11.2 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.1 times for the S&P 500. The stock was far cheaper on that measure at the end of June. At that time, shares traded at 6.8 times the same sales, marking the lowest multiple at any quarter end since fiscal 2018.

That price pays for growth. Zscaler increased its revenue by 25.4% to $3.35 billion in fiscal 2026, the twelve months to July 31, 2026. Management said on its September 3, 2026, earnings call that the results reflected increasing adoption of its Zero Trust platform. Buyers are not paying for a profit yet, however. Zscaler reported a net loss for fiscal 2026, so its price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful.

Moves like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

Zscaler Is Close To Breaking Even

Zscaler's loss is now small. The company posted an operating loss equal to 0.4% of revenue in fiscal Q4 2026, the three months to July 31. That is down from 4.3% in the same quarter a year earlier. For the full fiscal year, the operating loss settled at 3.6% of revenue, the smallest twelve-month loss relative to revenue at any quarter end since fiscal 2018.

The business also brings in cash alongside that reported loss. Zscaler generated $779 million in free cash flow for fiscal 2026, or 23.2% of revenue. That figure represents the cash left over after spending on equipment and on software Zscaler builds for its own use. Management expects capital spending to stay elevated in fiscal 2027 because components, especially memory, cost more.

Zscaler Expects Slower Growth In Fiscal 2027

The growth buyers are paying for is set to slow, according to management's own forecast. On the September 3 call, executives guided for fiscal 2027 revenue of $3.908 billion to $3.938 billion, representing growth of 16.6% to 17.5%. That pace is slower than the 25% Zscaler reported for fiscal 2026. Furthermore, part of that 25% came from buying Red Canary: without it, revenue grew 20%.
